packs.title: Gardens to the Skyline
packs.promise: Move from exhibition halls and garden carvings to coloured light, a memorial and a river seen from above.

q.s: Collect three clues from Dinosaur Walk without guessing the missing history.
st: Reach the main public entrance in the courtyard between the Royal Exhibition Building and museum, arrange or present valid general admission with the applicable fee or eligible free entry and use the current visitor map to find the open Dinosaur Walk gallery. Children under 12 must stay with an adult throughout the visit. If using member, senior, concession or student admission, present the relevant card and photo ID with the ticket.
Choose two mounted prehistoric animals. For each, record its displayed name and one visible difference in teeth, limbs, neck or tail.
Read a nearby label or reconstruction panel. Collect one statement that helps explain a feature you noticed, keeping the museum’s explanation separate from your own guess.
Write a three-item evidence list: two observed features and one labelled explanation. State whether a mount is a cast or fossil only if its label tells you.

q.s: Collect the planting choices that shape the Conservatory’s current room.
st: Check that the Conservatory is open for the current display before travelling. Enter through its ordinary visitor entrance during opening hours.
Collect three design choices from the display you see: one height contrast, one repeated colour or leaf shape, and one boundary between planting and visitor path.
Describe where each choice appears. Name a plant only when a label identifies it; a clear shape description is enough.
Choose which of the three most strongly guides your eye through the room, and explain your choice in one sentence.

q.s: Turn the coloured ceiling at NGV into a short piece of writing.
st: Enter NGV International through the St Kilda Road visitor entrance and follow the current map or staff directions to Gandel Hall, beneath Leonard French’s coloured-glass ceiling. Cloak backpacks, large bags and umbrellas. For notes, use pencil on paper no larger than A3, or write after leaving the room if staff direct you.
From a comfortable public position, choose two colours and one geometric shape you can actually see above you. Keep the route through the room clear.
Write four short lines that turn those three observations into a description of light. Avoid copying an artwork label or claiming what the artist intended.
Read your lines once and revise one word so the piece feels specific to the ceiling you saw. Record the room’s name with your writing.

packs.title: Within the Grid
packs.promise: Read the central city through market labels, two extraordinary rooms, shopping passages and moving images.

q.s: Collect the information traders choose to put beside what they sell.
st: Enter the trading market from an open Queen Street visitor approach and choose three different stalls with readable public product labels or signs.
Collect one piece of information from each: a product name, stated place of origin, material, ingredient or price. Do not guess an origin or require a trader to be interviewed.
Write which stall or aisle each clue came from and distinguish an advertised claim from something you observed yourself.
Choose the label that most helped you understand an unfamiliar product. Explain what it clarified; no purchase, taste test or handling is necessary.

q.s: Collect the floor and roof details that organise the Block Arcade.
st: Enter the open Block Arcade from Collins Street and find a place off the main walking line.
Collect one border pattern and one central pattern from the mosaic floor, without standing on a threshold or blocking the passage.
Look up from a stationary position and find one feature of the glass roof or dome that echoes, frames or contrasts with the floor.
Describe a three-part route for someone’s eyes: floor edge, floor centre, then roof. Use words or small simple shapes rather than copying a whole decorative panel.

q.s: Change a sequence at ACMI and notice how its meaning shifts.
st: Reach ACMI’s Flinders Street entrance by the signed Swanston Street crossing outside Flinders Street Station; the operator reports the corner crossing blocked. Enter the free exhibition and ask for the currently open Edit Line interactive. Children under 13 must stay with a parent or guardian over 18. Wait your turn; interactive availability and any bag cloaking follow staff directions.
Arrange a short sequence with the supplied story blocks, then change the order of two blocks and watch the result.
Write how the changed order altered what you expected, understood or felt. Do not copy dialogue or upload a clip; your written comparison is enough.

Create a three-shot sequence of your own in words: beginning, change and ending. If Edit Line is unavailable, choose an open exhibit about editing or sequence, read its interpretation and make two different orders for your own three written shots.
